case_name: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab

pages.text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Criminal Appeal No. 335 of 1978
Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others ... Appellants
versus
State of Punjab ... Respondent
Coram: Y.V. Chandrachud, C.J., P.N. Bhagwati, N.L. Untwalia, V.D. Tulzapurkar and A.P. Sen, JJ.
Judgment Dated: 09 April, 1980

CHANDRACHUD, C.J. delivered the Judgment of the Constitution Bench:
1. The questions involved in this appeal turn on the true scope and meaning of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. That section confers on the High Court and the Court of Session the power to grant anticipatory bail to persons apprehending arrest in non-bailable offences.

14. We find ourselves unable to accept the contention that the power under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure must be exercised only in exceptional cases. The High Court has observed that the power is of an extraordinary character and must be sparingly used. No such limitation is contained in the section. The Legislature conferred this power to protect personal liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution.

15. The right to personal liberty is too precious a value of our constitutional system to be subordinated to any consideration except the clear mandate of law. An arbitrary arrest causes irreparable harm to the reputation and self-esteem of a citizen.

35. In conclusion, the principles relating to the grant of anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC may be summarized as follows:
(a) The power to grant anticipatory bail is not unguided; it must be exercised according to judicial discretion considering the nature and seriousness of the accusation, the antecedents of the applicant, and the possibility of fleeing from justice.
(b) The operation of an order of anticipatory bail should not be mechanically limited to a specified duration or until the filing of the charge-sheet.
(c) Anticipatory bail can be granted even after the filing of the FIR, or before the FIR is lodged, provided there is a reasonable apprehension of arrest on accusation of having committed a non-bailable offence.
